Its assumptions allow N=1, where that vector cannot exist. An answer-only repair cannot prove the false universal construction. The new question preserves this instance for assessment, requests the plane only as a proved N>1 case, and separately asks for the exact endpoint action. That is an explicit first question-version2, not a hidden N>=2 assumption or an equivalent restatement.

The two-planar-mirrors convention is an algebraic fact about actual planes, not an assertion that such a plane exists on every search input; the question now tests that applicability. substantive_reconstruction.normalized_plane: For N>1, the marked basis vector g and b=(N-1)^(-1/2)sum_unmarked|x> have disjoint support, norm1 and inner product0. The uniform psi has coordinates(s,c), with s=1/sqrt(N)>0, c=sqrt((N-1)/N)>0 and s^2+c^2=1. Taking phi=arcsin(s) gives psi=sin(phi)g+cos(phi)b. Both reflections preserve this span because their defining projectors have their ranges in it or kill it appropriately. There is no need to infer an invariant subspace solely from source rhetoric or a division by sin(2phi).
substantive_reconstruction.ordered_algebra: R_g is diag(-1,1). The other reflection is2(s,c)(s,c)^T-I, so multiplying R_psi R_g, with the marked flip acting first, gives [[1-2s^2,2sc],[-2sc,2c^2-1]]. This is [[cos(2phi),sin(2phi)],[-sin(2phi),cos(2phi)]]. In the Cartesian coordinates whose ordered axes are(g,b) it is rotation by -2phi. In the alternative scalar parameterization sin(alpha)g+cos(alpha)b, alpha is measured from b towards g and increases by2phi. Those are the same action, not an inconsistent source sign or a swapped reflection order.
substantive_reconstruction.powers_and_phase: Multiplication of the last matrix by(sin(alpha),cos(alpha)) gives(sin(alpha+2phi),cos(alpha+2phi)). Starting at alpha=phi and inducting proves the exact all-k state formula. In particular the signed marked coefficient is sin((2k+1)phi). Its projected-vector norm is the absolute sine, and measurement probability is the sine squared. Late negative coefficients are permitted and no phase is discarded in the vector equality. A phase invisible to an isolated probability still matters to a controlled comparison, so this is stronger and more precise than only a probability curve.
substantive_reconstruction.endpoint_reconstruction: When N=1, the only state basis vector is g=psi. On this one-dimensional space R_psi=I and R_g=-I, so G=-I and G^k psi=(-1)^k g. The scalar formula survives since sin((2k+1)pi/2)=(-1)^k, but there is no unmarked sum to normalize, no orthogonal bad axis and no actual two-dimensional mirror geometry. Success is already1 at k0. N0 is impossible under the unique-mark promise. This is a separate operator calculation, not continuity used to manufacture a nonexistent vector.
